pointers.sentence: A request the middleware never saw raises `MessageFailure`, unless `fail_silently=True`, when the message is dropped and the call returns `None` (`django/contrib/messages/api.py:add_message`).
The flag excuses only the second; the documentation gives it to a reusable application whose host project may not install messages (`docs/ref/contrib/messages.txt`).

`SuccessMessageMixin.form_valid` calls a form view's own and then adds what `SuccessMessageMixin.get_success_message` returns, by default `SuccessMessageMixin.success_message` formatted with the form's cleaned data, as a success message, unless it comes out empty ([The form views](../views/editing.md)) (`django/contrib/messages/views.py:SuccessMessageMixin.form_valid`).
The five of `django/contrib/messages/constants.py` are `DEBUG` 10, `INFO` 20, `SUCCESS` 25, `WARNING` 30 and `ERROR` 40.

On a request without a storage `set_level` returns `False` (`django/contrib/messages/storage/base.py:BaseStorage._get_level`, `django/contrib/messages/storage/base.py:BaseStorage._set_level`, `django/contrib/messages/api.py:set_level`).

On a request without a storage `set_level` returns `False` (`django/contrib/messages/storage/base.py:BaseStorage._get_level`, `django/contrib/messages/storage/base.py:BaseStorage._set_level`, `django/contrib/messages/api.py:set_level`).

On a request without a storage `set_level` returns `False` (`django/contrib/messages/storage/base.py:BaseStorage._get_level`, `django/contrib/messages/storage/base.py:BaseStorage._set_level`, `django/contrib/messages/api.py:set_level`).

When `MESSAGE_STORAGE` names `FallbackStorage` or `SessionStorage`, that storage refuses to be made on a request without a session, and `get_level` raises `ImproperlyConfigured` (`django/contrib/messages/api.py:get_level`, `django/contrib/messages/storage/session.py:SessionStorage.__init__`).

When `MESSAGE_STORAGE` names `FallbackStorage` or `SessionStorage`, that storage refuses to be made on a request without a session, and `get_level` raises `ImproperlyConfigured` (`django/contrib/messages/api.py:get_level`, `django/contrib/messages/storage/session.py:SessionStorage.__init__`).
`get_level_tags` lays `MESSAGE_TAGS` over `DEFAULT_TAGS`, which names each of the five levels in lower case (`django/contrib/messages/utils.py:get_level_tags`).
The result is held in `LEVEL_TAGS`, a `SimpleLazyObject` in `django/contrib/messages/storage/base.py`, built when the first tag is asked for and kept for the life of the process.
So a `MESSAGE_TAGS` changed by `override_settings` is seen, and one assigned to the settings after the first tag is not (`django/contrib/messages/apps.py:update_level_tags`).

The admin gives `DEBUG` and `INFO` messages icons and styling of their own instead of `SUCCESS`'s; `ModelAdmin.message_user` adds at `INFO` by default ([The admin](../admin.md)) (`docs/releases/6.0.txt`).
A `Message` holds three things: `Message.level`, made an integer; `Message.message`, the text; and `Message.extra_tags` (`django/contrib/messages/storage/base.py:Message`).

`BaseStorage.add` drops an empty message and one below the level without a word, and otherwise appends a `Message` to the queue and sets `BaseStorage.added_new` (`django/contrib/messages/storage/base.py:BaseStorage.add`).

`len()` and `in` count and search both lists, loading the earlier messages, and leave `used` alone; and since no storage defines `__bool__`, Python's truth test of a storage is its length (`django/contrib/messages/storage/base.py:BaseStorage.__iter__`).
On the way out, `BaseStorage.update` stores what is left, in one of three cases (`django/contrib/messages/storage/base.py:BaseStorage.update`):
The documentation's way to keep messages after iterating over them is to set `used` back to `False` (`docs/ref/contrib/messages.txt`).

A template reaches the storage through the context processor `django/contrib/messages/context_processors.py:messages`, which gives it as `"messages"`, the storage itself (an empty list without the middleware), beside `"DEFAULT_MESSAGE_LEVELS"`, the five levels by name ([The context: `Context`, `RequestContext` and context processors](../templates/context.md)).

`MessageMiddleware.process_request` puts a storage on every request as `HttpRequest._messages`, made by `default_storage`, which imports the class `MESSAGE_STORAGE` names, `FallbackStorage` by default, at each call (`django/contrib/messages/storage/__init__.py:default_storage`).

`MessageMiddleware.process_response` calls the storage's `BaseStorage.update`, when the request has a storage. What it could not store is lost, and when `settings.DEBUG` is true the middleware raises `ValueError`, "Not all temporary messages could be stored." (`django/contrib/messages/middleware.py:MessageMiddleware.process_response`). The default storage leaves none, since `SessionStorage` keeps whatever it is given; `CookieStorage` alone leaves what its cookie cannot hold, and a run of it with `settings.DEBUG` true raised the error. `MessageMiddleware.async_capable` is false (6.2), so under ASGI the middleware runs synchronously ([Sync and async in one chain](../handlers/async.md)).
